html:
The map labels the land of Oman, in southeastern Arabia, "Mascat" in 1 BCE, after the port of Muscat that became its capital much later. In antiquity this was a land of mountain villages, date gardens and coastal ports.

In the 3rd millennium BCE Mesopotamian texts called it Magan, and it sent copper and stone to the Sumerian cities by sea. Its farmers watered their fields with falaj channels, which carried groundwater downhill from the mountains, a system still in use.

Persian empires, from the Achaemenids to the Parthians, held parts of the coast; the Persians later called it Mazun. Arab tribes such as the Azd moved in from Yemen in the early centuries CE. In the south, Dhofar exported frankincense through the port of Sumhuram. In the Middle Ages the town of Muscat rose to dominate the coast.
